name: X-37B OTV
best_known_for: USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — classified multi-year orbital missions, the only US spaceplane operational after the Shuttle's retirement. Looks like a quarter-scale Shuttle orbiter; lands itself on a runway
credit: Robotic mini-spaceplane (8.9 m long, ~5 t) — Boeing Phantom Works built two flight vehicles for USAF (transferred to USSF in 2019). Launches vertically (Atlas V 501 originally; SpaceX Falcon 9 from OTV-5 onwards; Falcon Heavy from OTV-7) and lands horizontally on Kennedy's former Shuttle runway. Carried as crewed-spacecraft category for its Shuttle-style aeroshell + lifting-body re-entry profile even though it flies uncrewed. Most payloads + orbital parameters are classified — typical mission durations stretch from 224 days (OTV-1, 2010) to a record 908 days (OTV-6, 2020–2022). Known declassified payloads include Hall-effect thruster tech demo, an Air Force Research Laboratory radio-frequency communication experiment, and a 1 W solar-power-to-microwave-beaming experiment (PRAM, OTV-6). As of 2026 has flown seven missions; OTV-7 ongoing.
